metadata.target_audience: Security professionals, penetration testers, red team operators

topics.title: Nmap Syntax and Target Specification
topics.content: Nmap (Network Mapper) is the industry-standard network discovery and security auditing tool. The basic command structure: nmap [Scan Type] [Options] [Target]. Target specification supports: single IPs (192.168.1.1), hostnames (target.example.com), CIDR notation (192.168.1.0/24 for 256 hosts), ranges (192.168.1.1-50), and octet ranges (192.168.0-255.1). Use -iL to read targets from file. Use --exclude and --excludefile to skip sensitive systems. Nmap performs host discovery before port scanning unless -Pn is specified.

topics.title: When to Use Nmap vs Other Tools
topics.content: Nmap excels at accuracy and deep enumeration but isn't always fastest. Masscan scans entire Internet in minutes but sacrifices accuracy. RustScan combines Masscan speed with Nmap integration. Zmap is for Internet-scale research. Use Nmap when you need: accurate version detection, vulnerability scanning via NSE, OS fingerprinting, stealth capabilities, or comprehensive analysis. Common workflow: Masscan for discovery, Nmap for deep enumeration of identified hosts.

examples.explanation: Masscan for fast discovery, Nmap for service detection

best_practices: Use right tool for the job

topics.title: Common Beginner Mistakes
topics.content: Most dangerous mistake: scanning wrong targets. Triple-check before pressing Enter. Running without root/sudo forces TCP Connect instead of faster SYN scans. Ignoring -Pn flag misses firewalled hosts. Using -T5 on production networks causes disruption. Trusting version banners without verification (Ubuntu backports patches without changing versions). Not saving output loses hours of work. Always use -oA to save all formats.

examples.explanation: Correct: sudo for privileges, -Pn for firewalled host

warnings: Wrong target can scan unauthorized networks
Version banners often inaccurate due to backporting
best_practices: Save output with -oA on every scan

topics.title: TCP SYN Scan (-sS)
topics.content: Default scan type with root privileges. Sends SYN packet, analyzes response without completing connection. SYN-ACK = open, RST = closed, no response = filtered. Called 'half-open' because connection never completes. Faster than TCP Connect, less logging on target. Requires root for raw socket access. Modern IDS still detects SYN scans but technique remains valuable for speed and reliability.

examples.explanation: Basic SYN scan of top 1000 ports
Full 65535 port SYN scan with minimum rate
SYN scan showing reason for port state

warnings: High-rate scans may trigger SYN flood protection

topics.title: TCP Connect Scan (-sT)
topics.content: Completes full TCP three-way handshake. Default when running without root. Uses OS connect() system call. Connections fully logged by target. Necessary for scanning through SOCKS proxies (proxychains). Slower than SYN scan. Use when root unavailable or proxy required.

topics.title: UDP Scan (-sU)
topics.content: Essential for complete assessment - critical services use UDP: DNS (53), SNMP (161), TFTP (69), NFS. UDP is connectionless - open ports often don't respond. ICMP port unreachable = closed, no response = open|filtered. Very slow due to ICMP rate limiting. Focus on high-value UDP ports rather than full scans. Combine with TCP: -sS -sU -p T:1-1000,U:53,161.

examples.explanation: Targeted high-value UDP with version detection

warnings: Heavy UDP can trigger rate limiting
best_practices: Run UDP in parallel with TCP

topics.title: FIN, NULL, and Xmas Scans
topics.content: Exploit RFC 793: closed ports must respond with RST to packets without SYN/RST/ACK flags. Open ports should ignore. FIN scan (-sF) sends FIN only. NULL scan (-sN) sends no flags. Xmas scan (-sX) sends FIN+PSH+URG. Main advantage: may bypass firewalls that only block SYN. CRITICAL: Does NOT work against Windows - they respond RST to everything. Only useful against Unix/Linux. Can only distinguish closed from open|filtered.

topics.title: ACK and Window Scans
topics.content: NOT for finding open ports - for mapping firewall rules. ACK scan (-sA) sends ACK packets. RST response = unfiltered (reaches host). No response = filtered. Cannot determine if ports are open. Window scan (-sW) examines RST window size for open/closed hints (unreliable, OS-dependent). Use to map what firewall allows, then SYN scan unfiltered ports.

examples.explanation: ACK scan to map firewall rules

warnings: Cannot determine if ports are open
best_practices: Follow up with SYN scans on unfiltered ports

topics.title: Port Ranges and Lists
topics.content: The -p flag specifies ports. Single: -p 22. Range: -p 1-1000. List: -p 22,80,443. Combined: -p 22,80,443,1000-2000. Full scan: -p- (all 65535). Protocol prefix: -p T:22,80,U:53,161 for TCP/UDP mix. --top-ports N scans N most common ports. --exclude-ports removes specific ports. Develop standard port sets: web (80,443,8080,8443), Windows (135,139,445,3389,5985), databases (1433,1521,3306,5432,27017).

examples.explanation: Full 65535 port scan with aggressive rate

best_practices: Create standard port sets for common scenarios

topics.title: Fast Scan vs Full Scan Strategies
topics.content: Fast scan (-F) reduces to 100 ports vs default 1000. Full scan (-p-) covers all 65535. Strategy depends on time, stealth, and thoroughness needs. External perimeters: be thorough. Large internal networks: fast initial sweep, then full scan interesting hosts. Hybrid: --top-ports 3000 balances speed and coverage. Multi-phase: -F across network, identify targets, -p- those hosts.

topics.title: Timing Templates (T0-T5)
topics.content: T0 (Paranoid): 5 min between probes, evades IDS, impractical (80+ hours for 1000 ports). T1 (Sneaky): 15 sec intervals, still evades time-based IDS. T2 (Polite): 0.4 sec intervals, reduces network load. T3 (Normal): Default, balanced. T4 (Aggressive): Faster, assumes reliable network, good for internal. T5 (Insane): Maximum speed, misses ports on slow hosts, lab only.
warnings: T5 misses ports on slow hosts

topics.title: Rate Limiting and Parallelization
topics.content: --max-rate caps packets/second (e.g., --max-rate 100 for IDS evasion). --min-rate forces minimum rate. --min-hostgroup/--max-hostgroup control parallel hosts. --max-parallelism controls probes per host. --host-timeout abandons slow hosts (e.g., --host-timeout 30m). --max-retries limits retransmissions (reduce from 10 to 2-3 for speed).

examples.explanation: Limited retries and timeout for efficiency
examples.use_case: Large network with some unresponsive hosts

best_practices: Use --max-rate to stay under IDS thresholds

topics.title: SMB Vulnerability Scripts
topics.content: Critical for Windows networks. smb-vuln-ms17-010 detects EternalBlue (CVE-2017-0144) - WannaCry/NotPetya exploit, RCE on Windows Vista through 10, Server 2008-2016. smb-vuln-cve-2020-0796 detects SMBGhost in SMB 3.1.1 compression (Windows 10 1903/1909). Other scripts: smb-vuln-ms08-067 (Conficker), smb-vuln-cve-2017-7494 (SambaCry for Linux). Scripts are safe - detect without exploiting. Use --script-args=unsafe=1 for aggressive checks (may crash services).
best_practices: Run smb-vuln-* on all Windows with 445 open

topics.title: SSL/TLS Vulnerability Scripts
topics.content: ssl-heartbleed detects CVE-2014-0160 (Heartbleed) - OpenSSL buffer over-read leaking memory including private keys. Affects OpenSSL 1.0.1-1.0.1f. ssl-poodle checks CVE-2014-3566 - SSLv3 CBC attack, mitigation is disabling SSLv3. ssl-ccs-injection detects CVE-2014-0224 - OpenSSL CCS MITM. ssl-dh-params checks for weak DH/Logjam. ssl-enum-ciphers grades all cipher suites A-F.
warnings: Heavy TLS scanning causes server load
Some scripts need specific TLS versions
best_practices: Scan all TLS ports not just 443
Combine with testssl.sh for deep analysis

topics.title: HTTP Vulnerability Scripts
topics.content: http-slowloris-check detects CVE-2007-6750 (Slowloris DoS) - holds partial connections to exhaust resources. CAUTION: can cause actual DoS. http-shellshock tests CVE-2014-6271 (Shellshock) - Bash RCE via CGI. Tests /cgi-bin/*.cgi paths. http-vuln-cve2017-5638 (Struts RCE), http-vuln-cve2015-1635 (MS15-034 IIS HTTP.sys RCE), http-vuln-cve2014-3704 (Drupalgeddon).
best_practices: Identify web tech before running specific scripts
Use dedicated web scanners for thorough testing
Avoid DoS scripts without explicit authorization

topics.title: RDP Vulnerability Scripts
topics.content: rdp-vuln-ms12-020 detects CVE-2012-0002 - pre-auth RCE in RDP. BlueKeep (CVE-2019-0708) is critical pre-auth RCE affecting Windows 7, Server 2008, XP, Server 2003 - wormable like WannaCry. rdp-ntlm-info extracts system info without creds: computer name, domain, OS version. rdp-enum-encryption checks NLA status which affects exploitability.
warnings: Some scripts may cause BSOD on old systems
best_practices: Scan all Windows for RDP exposure
Check NLA status for exploitability assessment

topics.title: SMB Enumeration Scripts
topics.content: smb-os-discovery extracts Windows version, computer name, domain via null session. smb-enum-shares lists accessible shares including admin shares (C$, ADMIN$). smb-enum-users enumerates usernames via SAM/LSA queries. smb-protocols identifies SMB versions (SMB1 = legacy/vulnerable). smb-security-mode checks signing - disabled signing enables relay attacks. smb-enum-sessions shows active logins.
warnings: smb-enum-users may trigger failed logon events
best_practices: Note SMB signing status for relay attacks
Use authenticated enumeration after getting creds

topics.title: HTTP Enumeration Scripts
topics.content: http-enum performs directory/file brute-forcing: /admin, /backup, /phpmyadmin, etc. http-methods tests supported methods - dangerous ones: PUT, DELETE, TRACE. http-headers analyzes response headers for version info and missing security headers. http-title extracts page titles for quick app identification. http-vhosts discovers virtual hosts. http-generator finds CMS signatures.

examples.use_case: Quick identification of all web apps
Finding additional apps on shared hosting

best_practices: Follow up with dedicated web tools

topics.title: LDAP and Active Directory Enumeration
topics.content: ldap-rootdse queries Root DSE for directory config: naming contexts, domain functional level, AD topology. ldap-search performs custom queries - enumerate users, groups, computers, OUs. Anonymous binding often allows reading many attributes. Can reveal password policies, Domain Admins members, trust relationships.
warnings: Anonymous LDAP often restricted in modern AD

categories.name: NSE Scripts - Authentication and Brute Force

topics.title: Safe Credential Testing
topics.content: Account lockout is primary risk - typically 3-5 failed attempts, 30 min lockout. Safe approach: password spraying (1 password x many users vs many passwords x 1 user). Use brute.delay for rate limiting: --script-args brute.delay=5s. Default credential scripts safer than full wordlists - test root:root, admin:admin first. Coordinate with client about policies before testing.

examples.explanation: Default creds only, stop on first success

warnings: SMB brute on AD locks legitimate users
Document all testing for legal protection
best_practices: Use password spraying vs brute force

topics.title: Packet Fragmentation
topics.content: Splits probes into fragments that some IDS/firewalls fail to reassemble correctly. -f uses 8-byte fragments, -ff uses 16-byte. --mtu sets custom size (multiple of 8). Modern IDS handles fragmentation but combined with other techniques increases evasion. May cause packet loss. Some firewalls block all fragments. Works best for initial SYN scans, not detailed enumeration.
warnings: May not work with version detection/scripts
best_practices: Test effectiveness before relying on it

topics.title: Decoy Scanning and Spoofing
topics.content: Decoys (-D) send forged packets from multiple IPs: -D decoy1,decoy2,ME,decoy3. RND:10 uses 10 random decoys. Target sees scans from multiple sources. Idle scan (-sI) uses zombie host for complete anonymity - never sends packets from your IP. Source port (--source-port 53) may bypass firewalls allowing DNS. MAC spoofing (--spoof-mac) works on local segment only.
warnings: Decoy IPs may trace to innocents
best_practices: Use live, diverse IPs as decoys

topics.title: OS Fingerprinting Techniques
topics.content: Nmap identifies OS by analyzing TCP/IP stack implementation: initial TTL, window size, TCP options ordering, IP ID generation, responses to malformed packets. -O enables detection. --osscan-guess shows low-confidence matches. --osscan-limit skips hosts without required port states. -A combines OS detection, version detection, scripts, and traceroute. Database contains 5000+ signatures. CPE identifiers (cpe:/o:microsoft:windows_server_2019) enable vulnerability database correlation.

topics.title: Version Detection Mechanics
topics.content: -sV identifies services and versions via banner grabbing and active probes matched against nmap-service-probes database. --version-intensity 0-9 controls thoroughness (default 7). --version-light (2) for fast, --version-all (9) for thorough. Output includes service name, application, version, sometimes OS/patch info. CRITICAL: Banners can be spoofed; Ubuntu backports patches without changing version strings. Always verify critical versions.

examples.explanation: Fast scan with light version detection

warnings: Ubuntu/Debian backports mean version may not reflect patches
best_practices: Verify critical versions through other means

topics.title: Output Formats and Automation
topics.content: -oN normal human-readable text. -oX XML for tool integration (Metasploit, custom scripts). -oG grepable single-line-per-host format. -oA creates all three with same base filename - ALWAYS USE THIS. --resume continues interrupted scans from XML. Parse grepable with grep/awk, XML with Python xml.etree or python-nmap library.

examples.command: grep '445/open' scan.gnmap | awk '{print $2}' | xargs nmap -p445 --script smb-vuln-*

warnings: Without -o flags, results lost if terminal closes
best_practices: Develop extraction scripts for common tasks

topics.title: Common Errors and Solutions
topics.content: Permission errors: 'requires root privileges' means use sudo. No hosts/ports found: use -Pn for firewalled targets. Timeouts: increase --host-timeout, reduce parallelism. --packet-trace shows every packet (use on single hosts). -v/-vv/-vvv increase verbosity. -d/-dd for debug. --reason shows why ports classified as open/closed/filtered. False negatives: slow down timing, reduce parallelism, try different scan types.

examples.explanation: Very verbose with no host discovery

topics.title: Safe SMB Scanning Without Lockouts
topics.content: SAFE scripts (no lockouts): smb-protocols, smb-security-mode, smb-os-discovery, smb-vuln-* (vuln checks don't auth), smb-enum-shares. DANGEROUS: smb-brute, smb-enum-users aggressive mode. Windows lockout typically 5 failures, 30 min duration. Null session: --script-args smbusername="",smbpassword="". SMB signing disabled = relay attack opportunity - critical finding.

best_practices: Verify lockout policy before cred testing

topics.title: SSL/TLS Analysis and Certificate Inspection
topics.content: ssl-enum-ciphers grades ciphers A-F, tests SSL2/3, TLS 1.0-1.3. Weak: export ciphers, DES/3DES, RC4, NULL. Modern requires TLS 1.2+ with ECDHE and AES-GCM. ssl-cert extracts: subject, issuer, validity, SANs. Flag: expired certs, self-signed, internal hostnames in SANs. PCI DSS requires TLS 1.2 minimum.

examples.explanation: All SSL analysis on HTTPS ports

topics.title: Database Enumeration and Default Credentials
topics.content: MySQL (3306): mysql-info, mysql-enum, mysql-databases, mysql-brute. Common: root with blank password. MSSQL (1433/1434): ms-sql-info, ms-sql-empty-password, ms-sql-brute. Check blank SA. PostgreSQL (5432): pgsql-brute. MongoDB (27017): mongodb-info, mongodb-databases. Often no auth by default. Redis (6379): redis-info. Defaults to no auth, permits dangerous commands including potential RCE.

examples.explanation: MSSQL info and blank SA check

warnings: Some databases lack lockout but may block IPs

topics.title: SSH Enumeration and Backporting Verification
topics.content: CRITICAL: SSH version banners DO NOT reflect actual patch status on Ubuntu/Debian due to backporting. OpenSSH 7.2p2 on Ubuntu may be fully patched. Scripts: ssh-auth-methods (auth types without login), ssh-hostkey (key fingerprints), ssh2-enum-algos (ciphers/algorithms). To verify actual patches: use ssh-audit tool, check dpkg -l openssh-server, test for specific CVEs. CVE-2016-6210 and CVE-2018-15473 allow user enumeration.

examples.explanation: SSH brute with delay (use with caution)

warnings: Banner version DOES NOT indicate patch status
Ubuntu backports security patches without version change
ssh-brute may be blocked by fail2ban
User enumeration CVEs require specific testing
best_practices: Never trust SSH version banner for vulnerability assessment
Test specific CVEs rather than relying on version

topics.title: SSH User Enumeration Vulnerabilities
topics.content: CVE-2018-15473 (OpenSSH < 7.7): Timing-based user enumeration via malformed packets. Invalid users get immediate rejection; valid users trigger delayed response. CVE-2016-6210 (OpenSSH < 7.3): Similar timing attack via long passwords. Both require specific tools/scripts for exploitation. Nmap's ssh-brute may indicate valid users via response timing but dedicated tools like ssh-user-enum are more reliable.

examples.use_case: Determine if user enum CVEs apply

warnings: Version banner doesn't confirm vulnerability due to backporting
best_practices: Verify with dedicated user enumeration tools
Check actual patch status not just version

topics.title: External Network Reconnaissance Workflow
topics.content: Phase 1: Passive recon (DNS, OSINT, certificates). Phase 2: Port discovery with stealth (-T2, --max-rate 100). Phase 3: Service enumeration (-sV) on discovered ports. Phase 4: Vulnerability scanning (NSE scripts). Phase 5: Manual verification of findings. Use slow timing for external scans to avoid detection. Prioritize: exposed management interfaces, VPN endpoints, web apps, email servers.

examples.explanation: Stealthy full port scan of external perimeter

warnings: External scanning may violate laws without authorization
Client firewall logs will show activity

topics.title: Internal Network Scanning Workflow
topics.content: Internal scanning can be faster (-T4) since stealth less critical. Phase 1: Host discovery (nmap -sn). Phase 2: Quick port scan (-F or --top-ports). Phase 3: Detailed scan of interesting hosts (-p-). Phase 4: Service/vulnerability scanning. Prioritize: Domain Controllers (88,389,445), file servers (445), databases (1433,3306), web apps (80,443), management (22,3389,5985).

examples.explanation: Host discovery on large internal network

warnings: Still need authorization for internal scans
best_practices: Coordinate with IT for sensitive systems

topics.title: Integration with Metasploit
topics.content: Metasploit imports Nmap XML directly. In msfconsole: db_nmap runs Nmap and auto-imports. db_import loads existing XML. hosts/services commands query imported data. vulns shows vulnerability correlations. Workflow: Nmap discovery → Import to MSF → Search exploits → Validate → Exploit. Use workspaces to organize different engagements.
best_practices: Import all Nmap scans for correlation

topics.title: Active Directory Enumeration
topics.content: Identify DCs via DNS (nslookup -type=srv _ldap._tcp.dc._msdcs.domain), port 88 (Kerberos), or 389 (LDAP). Key ports: 88 (Kerberos), 389/636 (LDAP/S), 445 (SMB), 464 (Kpasswd), 3268/3269 (Global Catalog). Use ldap-rootdse for domain info, smb-os-discovery for computer accounts, smb-enum-users for domain users if null sessions allowed.
warnings: Heavy AD scanning detected by SIEM

topics.title: Ubuntu/Debian Backporting Explained
topics.content: CRITICAL CONCEPT: Ubuntu and Debian backport security patches to older package versions WITHOUT changing the version number. OpenSSH 7.2p2 on Ubuntu 16.04 may have ALL security patches applied despite showing an 'old' version. This causes massive false positives in vulnerability scanners that rely on version banners. NEVER report vulnerabilities based solely on version numbers for Debian-based systems. Verification required: dpkg -l <package>, apt-cache policy <package>, or check Ubuntu Security Notices.

examples.explanation: Check actual installed package version with patch level
examples.use_case: Verify OpenSSH patch status on target

warnings: Version banners are UNRELIABLE on Ubuntu/Debian
best_practices: NEVER report version-based vulns without verification
Use dpkg -l on target if you have access

topics.title: Version Banner vs Actual Patches
topics.content: Version banners reflect upstream version, not security status. Examples: OpenSSH 7.2p2 banner on Ubuntu 18.04 has CVE-2016-6210 patched. Apache 2.4.29 on Ubuntu has CVE-2021-41773 patched. PHP 7.2.24 on Debian has numerous CVEs patched. Verification methods: Package manager queries (dpkg, rpm), security tool outputs (ssh-audit, testssl.sh), vendor security advisories, manual CVE testing.

examples.explanation: Comprehensive SSH security analysis beyond version

warnings: Never trust version alone for vulnerability status
Automated scanners produce many false positives
Manual verification essential for accurate reporting

topics.title: Common False Positive Examples
topics.content: OpenSSH on Ubuntu: Banner shows 7.6p1, scanner reports CVE-2018-15473 - VERIFY with ssh-audit, likely patched. Apache on Debian: Banner shows 2.4.25, scanner reports CVE-2021-41773 - CHECK dpkg -l apache2, likely patched. PHP on Ubuntu: Banner shows 7.2, scanner reports dozens of CVEs - VERIFY with php -v and apt-cache policy. OpenSSL: Banner shows 1.1.1, scanner reports Heartbleed - VERIFY version carefully, Heartbleed affects 1.0.1-1.0.1f only.

examples.explanation: Compare Nmap banner with actual package

warnings: Client IT teams will dispute false positives
Version-based scanning is fast but inaccurate
best_practices: Use actual exploitation checks where safe

topics.title: Verification Tools and Techniques
topics.content: ssh-audit: Comprehensive SSH analysis - algorithms, key exchange, actual CVE status beyond banners. testssl.sh: Deep SSL/TLS testing - all vulnerabilities, cipher analysis, certificate issues. nuclei: Template-based vulnerability verification. Manual testing: netcat/telnet for banner grabbing, curl for HTTP, openssl s_client for TLS. Package verification: dpkg -l (Debian), rpm -qa (RHEL), requires target access.
warnings: Some verification tools may crash services
Manual testing takes time but is most reliable
best_practices: Prefer detection over exploitation when possible
